## Suitability and scope

OMIP-111 is suitable for an external **agreement comparison** of cytokine
gating methods. The deposit includes ten matched mice (five C57BL/6, five
BALB/c), each with a Brefeldin A control and a mitogen plus Brefeldin A tube,
two author-supplied FlowJo workspaces, and a sample-key spreadsheet. The 18
single-colour/unstained reference files are excluded from the biological
comparison. The full-panel FCS files are already spectrally unmixed.

The [OMIP-111 publication](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC12758606/)
describes 6-hour PMA/ionomycin stimulation and gating cytokines in conventional
non-naïve CD4/CD8 T cells. We reconstruct the authors' lymphocyte, singlet,
live CD45 and lineage gates with their own definitions. The authors' cytokine
gates (Supplementary Figures S11 and S12) are rectangles on cytokine versus
CD44, drawn inside a non-naïve gate on CD44 versus CD62L, and their published
frequencies are the counts in those rectangles divided by the non-naïve count.
The non-naïve gate keeps CD44-high cells (CD44 above 18,396) and also
CD62L-low cells at any CD44 level. Stimulation sheds CD62L, so 99–100% of
stimulated CD4 and CD8 T cells fall in it, against 15–39% of control cells: as
a comparison parent it pairs a nearly unselected stimulated tube with a
memory-enriched control. The CD44 side of each cytokine rectangle restores
the memory restriction in the stimulated tube.

The primary comparison therefore uses a **CD44+ parent for each cytokine**,
following the authors' gating path exactly: the non-naïve cells whose CD44
lies within the CD44 interval of that tube's author gate for the cytokine,
compared on the authors' own display scale. The intervals are the same in all
20 tubes; their lower bounds are, in raw units, 15,418 (CD4 IFNγ), 17,489 (CD4
IL-2 and IL-4/5), 18,396 (CD4 TNF), 18,867 (CD4 IL-17A), 9,345 (CD8 IFNγ),
10,071 (CD8 IL-2) and 11,129 (CD8 TNF); the upper bounds exclude no
cytokine-positive cells. Within its parent the author gate reduces to a
cytokine cutoff. Where an interval starts below CD44 18,396 (CD4 IFNγ and
IL-2/IL-4/5, every CD8 cytokine), the non-naïve gate still depends on CD62L in
that band: control-tube cells there are excluded when CD62L-high, while their
stimulated counterparts have shed CD62L and are kept. The validation section
reports how much of each parent this removes, by tube. Every method gates
each cytokine on the same parent cells, and StimGate runs once per cytokine. CD4 is evaluated for IFNγ, IL-2, TNF,
**combined IL-4/5**, and IL-17A; CD8 is evaluated for IFNγ, IL-2 and TNF,
matching the cytokine reference gates supplied in the workspaces.

Manual gating is an imperfect reference, not biological ground truth. This
small, strongly stimulated mouse dataset cannot establish performance on rare
antigen-specific human responses. IL-17A and IL-4/5 are particularly sparse;
percentage-point differences remain interpretable when relative errors would
be unstable or undefined. Frequencies below refer to each tube's own
cytokine-specific CD44-high parent, so they are larger than the published
frequencies of the non-naïve gate; the CSVs keep the published-scale frequencies alongside. The supplement's
Mice 1–5 are files M1–M5.
Strains are analysed separately, avoiding shared gates across different panels
(NK1.1 versus NKp46) and potentially different display transformations.

## Setup and scientific settings

Run from the package root:

```bash
RUN_SIMULATIONS=true RUN_PLOTS=true quarto render analysis/14-real-compare-omip111.qmd
```

`RUN_PREPROCESSING` and `RUN_METHODS` override the umbrella computation flag.
To redraw validated saved results, use `RUN_SIMULATIONS=false RUN_PLOTS=true`.
The workspace importer requires Python with `flowkit==1.3.2`. On this workspace
it is installed in the isolated `cache/omip111-python` environment. Override its
Python path with `OMIP111_PYTHON` when needed. Create an equivalent environment
with `python3 -m venv --system-site-packages <path>` and
`<path>/bin/python -m pip install flowkit==1.3.2`.
F-beta requires Python with NumPy, selected through `RETICULATE_PYTHON` where
needed. Missing method dependencies fail before any method runs.

```{r}

#| include: false

stopifnot(file.exists(file.path(root_dir, "DESCRIPTION")))
knitr::opts_knit$set(root.dir = root_dir)
scripts_r_dir <- file.path(root_dir, "scripts", "r")
source(file.path(scripts_r_dir, "analysis-runtime.R"))
isolated_library <- .analysis_project_dir("cache", "omip111-R-library", root_dir, create = FALSE)
if (dir.exists(isolated_library)) .libPaths(c(isolated_library, .libPaths()))
source(file.path(scripts_r_dir, "analysis-plot-style.R"))
source(file.path(scripts_r_dir, "acs_cytof-helper.R"))
source(file.path(scripts_r_dir, "acs_cytof-gate.R"))
```

```{r}
#| label: scientific-settings
scientific_settings <- list(
  semantics = "omip111-v12", seed = 20261009L,
  preprocessing = list(reference = "author cytokine-by-CD44 gates on each gate's CD44 interval",
    cofactor = 150, parentRelativeTolerance = 0.02,
    frequencyTolerancePp = 0.1),
  control = list(bwMtd = "nrd0", bwScope = "cytokine", bwNcellMax = 1e4,
    bwNcellMin = 1e4, bwFallback = "auto", bwMin = "none", bwMax = "none",
    biasUnsFactor = 1, gateCombn = "min", clusterGates = TRUE,
    calcCytPosGates = FALSE, minCell = 100, locThresholdMethod = "cap",
    locShiftedPeakRef = TRUE),
  comparators = list(
    fbeta = .acsCytofComparatorSettings("fbeta_default")$params,
    tailgate = .acsCytofComparatorSettings("tailgate_simulation_allcells")$params))
```

Before fitting any method, raw unmixed cytokine intensities are transformed
with `asinh(x / 150)`, retaining negative values and casting to the same float32
precision used by the package. Cofactor 150 is a conventional starting point
for flow cytometry ([workflow reference](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC5473464/));
it is fixed here, not tuned against the manual reference. The authors' display
transformations are used only for reconstructing their gates. The FlowKit
import differs slightly from the stored FlowJo counts, so exact event
reproduction is not claimed. Guardrails require every lineage and non-naïve
count to agree within 2%. A tube whose reconstructed cytokine frequency, on the
published non-naïve scale, differs from FlowJo's by more than 0.1 percentage
points is not scored for that marker. These are import checks, not statements
of biological accuracy; actual differences are reported below. The reference
audit CSV also keeps a cytokine-only cut (the rectangle's lower cytokine bound
applied to every parent cell, ignoring the non-naïve gate) for comparison.

StimGate uses shared per-cytokine bandwidths, bandwidth-based unstimulated bias,
threshold sharing, with cytokine-positive refinement off (one gate per
cytokine, as the author gates and the comparators have) and the same control
settings as the ACS real-data analysis, plus the shifted-peak rule
(`locShiftedPeakRef = TRUE`) used in every flow-cytometry analysis. StimGate
normally starts looking for responding cells one third of a left-window width
above the higher of the stimulated and unstimulated main peaks. After
PMA/ionomycin most cells make TNF, so the stimulated main peak is itself made
of responding cells. When the stimulated main peak lies more than two
bandwidths to the right of the unstimulated main peak, the rule starts the
search above the unstimulated peak instead. Because each cytokine has its own
parent, StimGate runs separately for each cytokine (threshold sharing still
spans the five mice of a strain). We score its final `loc_minClust` counts,
which equal the plain `x > gate` counts.

F-beta uses β = 0.8, θ = 2, smoothing width 10 and automatic bin count.
The existing Richards implementation uses common histogram edges spanning
both tubes, rather than the original unstimulated-only range. Tailgate uses
the settings selected in the simulations (Analyses 6 and 7): the stimulated
distribution, automatic bandwidth, automatic derivative tolerance (1% of the
largest absolute first derivative of the density) and a bias of 0.15 added to
the cutpoint. They were chosen on simulated data, not on these author gates.
We retain zero and negative fluorescence values, with no ACS-specific CyTOF
zero-spike adjustments. Every comparator
threshold is applied to both matched tubes using strict `x > threshold`.
Genuine no-cutpoint outcomes retain an explicitly labelled empty-gate fallback;
runtime errors retain missing estimates and counts.

The main estimand is **unclipped** stimulated minus unstimulated frequency.
Negative estimates are retained. The manual reference is the authors' own
cytokine-by-CD44 gate in each tube: its counts are the published counts,
divided by that cytokine's CD44-high parent rather than the non-naïve gate.
The reference is an imperfect manual reference, not biological truth. Reference
subtraction uses each tube's own author gate; automated subtraction uses the
stimulated sample's final gating rule in both tubes. Errors are expressed in
percentage points.
Each mouse is the independent biological unit; markers and cell populations
from one mouse are repeated outcomes, not extra independent replicates.

## Preparation and method execution

```{r}
#| label: run-analysis
#| include: false
if (run_preprocessing) .omip111Preprocess(path_raw, path_prepared, scientific_settings$preprocessing, path_python, path_importer)
if (run_methods) {
  if (!file.exists(file.path(path_prepared, "COMPLETE"))) stop("Validated OMIP-111 inputs are missing.")
  prepared_inputs <- readRDS(file.path(path_prepared, "inputs.rds"))
  .omip111Run(prepared_inputs, path_results, scientific_settings, path_fbeta)
}
if (!file.exists(file.path(path_results, "COMPLETE"))) stop("Complete OMIP-111 results are missing; run the analysis first.")
comparison_object <- readRDS(file.path(path_results, "result.rds"))
if (!identical(comparison_object$settings, scientific_settings)) stop("Saved scientific settings differ; rerun methods.")
comparison_results <- comparison_object$results
comparison_summary <- .omip111Summary(comparison_results)
```

## Validation and method coverage

```{r}
#| label: validation
#| results: asis
if (isTRUE(run_plots)) {
  prepared_inputs <- readRDS(file.path(path_prepared, "inputs.rds"))
  if (!identical(prepared_inputs$manifest, comparison_object$preprocessing)) {
    stop("Prepared inputs differ from the method comparison manifest.")
  }
  cat("FlowKit import audited **", nrow(prepared_inputs$validation),
    "** population counts against the saved FlowJo counts. Maximum absolute count difference across the full tree: **",
    max(abs(prepared_inputs$validation$difference)), "**.\n\n", sep = "")
  ref_audit <- prepared_inputs$references
  cat("Maximum lineage and non-naïve count differences: **",
    round(100 * max(abs(ref_audit$importedLineage / ref_audit$flowjoLineage - 1)), 3), "%** and **",
    round(100 * max(abs(ref_audit$importedNonNaive / ref_audit$flowjoNonNaive - 1)), 3),
    "%**. Maximum per-tube author cytokine-frequency difference (published non-naïve scale): **",
    round(max(abs(ref_audit$frequencyDifferencePp)), 4), " percentage points**; **",
    sum(!ref_audit$referenceAccepted), "** tube/marker reference(s) exceed the 0.1 limit and are not scored.\n\n", sep = "")
  parent_shrink <- ref_audit |>
    dplyr::mutate(condition = ifelse(grepl("_Stim_", .data$sample), "stimulated", "control"),
      retained = 100 * .data$importedParent / .data$lineageCd44Parent) |>
    dplyr::group_by(.data$population, .data$marker, .data$condition) |>
    dplyr::summarise(min_retained_pct = min(.data$retained), max_retained_pct = max(.data$retained),
      .groups = "drop")
  cat("Share of each CD44 interval's T cells kept by the authors' non-naïve gate (the CD44+ parent), ",
    "by population, cytokine and tube (range over mice):\n\n", sep = "")
  print(knitr::kable(parent_shrink, digits = 1))
  .analysis_report_table(ref_audit, c(fig_key, "reference-audit.csv"),
    "Author 2-D gate reproduction against FlowJo, with each cytokine's CD44 parent and cytokine-only counts.", root_dir)
  .analysis_report_table(prepared_inputs$validation, c(fig_key, "gate-validation.csv"), "Gate-count validation.", root_dir)
  .analysis_report_table(prepared_inputs$populations, c(fig_key, "parent-populations.csv"), "Parent-population cell counts.", root_dir)
  coverage <- comparison_results |>
    dplyr::group_by(.data$method) |>
    dplyr::summarise(intended = dplyr::n(), finite = sum(is.finite(.data$propBs)),
      reference_eligible = sum(.data$referenceAccepted),
      errors = sum(!is.na(.data$error)), fallbacks = sum(.data$thresholdFallbackUsed, na.rm = TRUE),
      .groups = "drop")
  print(knitr::kable(coverage))
  .analysis_report_table(comparison_results, c(fig_key, "comparison.csv"), "Every individual comparison, including failure and threshold provenance.", root_dir)
  .analysis_report_table(comparison_summary, c(fig_key, "summary.csv"), "Per-strain, population and marker errors with finite-mouse coverage.", root_dir)
}
```

## Reproduction of Supplementary Figures S11 and S12

Supplementary Figures S11 (C57BL/6) and S12 (BALB/c) of the OMIP-111 paper
show, for each mouse's stimulated tube, every non-naïve CD4 T cell on CD44
against each cytokine, with the authors' cytokine gate and its frequency
(count over the non-naïve count). They are redrawn here from the prepared
data: the reconstructed non-naïve gate and author gates, and the analysis
scale `asinh(raw / 150)` on both axes (ticks in raw units), rather than
FlowJo's display transforms. Points are coloured by the number of cells in
their bin, as in FlowJo's pseudocolour plots. Red labels are the reconstructed
frequencies; the table below compares them with the FlowJo counts behind the
printed figures.

```{r}
#| label: author-figures
#| results: asis
#| echo: false
if (isTRUE(run_plots)) {
  author_dir <- .analysis_fig_dir(c(fig_key, "author-figures"), root_dir)
  author_check <- list()
  for (strain in c("C57", "BALB")) {
    figure_name <- if (strain == "C57") "S11" else "S12"
    cat("\n\n### Figure ", figure_name, " (", if (strain == "C57") "C57BL/6" else "BALB/c", ")\n\n", sep = "")
    figure_data <- .omip111AuthorFigureData(prepared_inputs, strain, scientific_settings$preprocessing$cofactor)
    p <- .omip111AuthorFigure(figure_data, scientific_settings$preprocessing$cofactor)
    path_png <- file.path(author_dir, paste0(figure_name, "-", strain, ".png"))
    ggplot2::ggsave(path_png, p, width = 30, height = 30, units = "cm", dpi = 150, bg = "white")
    cat("![Figure ", figure_name, " reproduced](", knitr::image_uri(path_png), ")\n\n", sep = "")
    author_check[[strain]] <- dplyr::mutate(figure_data$gates, strain = strain)
  }
  author_check <- dplyr::bind_rows(author_check)
  author_check$differencePp <- author_check$frequency - author_check$flowjoFrequency
  cat("Reconstructed against FlowJo frequencies over all ", nrow(author_check),
    " panels: maximum absolute difference **", round(max(abs(author_check$differencePp)), 3),
    " percentage points**.\n\n", sep = "")
  .analysis_report_table(author_check[c("strain", "column", "marker", "nonNaive", "frequency",
    "flowjoFrequency", "differencePp")], c(fig_key, "author-figures.csv"),
    "Reconstructed and FlowJo frequencies for every panel of Figures S11 and S12.", root_dir)
}
```

## Automated and manual gates by fit population

Every method is fitted on two populations: **CD44+**, each cytokine's
CD44-high parent (the CD44 interval of the authors' gate for that cytokine,
the primary comparison in this analysis), and **non-naïve**, every cell in the
authors' non-naïve gate, as the authors' figures show. The non-naïve gate
holds 99–100% of stimulated T cells but only 15–39% of control T cells (the
stimulation sheds CD62L), so a non-naïve fit compares tubes of very different
composition. The same gate is applied to both tubes.

For each fit population there are two figures per strain and T-cell
population, in the layout of Supplementary Figures S11 and S12 (cytokines in
rows, mice in columns; stimulated tube only):

- **Bivariate**: every non-naïve cell, CD44 against the cytokine, shaded grey
  by density. The grey frame is the authors' rectangle, with its cytokine
  cutoff dashed black. Each method's gate is its threshold line (cells
  strictly above it are positive) drawn across the rectangle's CD44 interval
  only, coloured by method; a line below the rectangle lies below the authors'
  cutoff. Labels: **% of all non-naïve cells**, counting as positive the
  cells inside the rectangle's CD44 interval above the gate (the authors' CD44
  restriction applies whichever population the gate was fitted on).
- **Univariate**: histograms of the cytokine in its CD44+ parent (square-root
  count scale), with each method's threshold and the authors' cytokine cutoff
  (dashed). Labels: **% of the CD44+ parent**; the manual figure is the
  authors' 2-D gate count over that parent. The x axis extends to show every gate.

Frequencies are stimulated-tube percentages without background subtraction.

```{r}
#| label: method-author-figures
#| results: asis
#| echo: false
if (isTRUE(run_plots)) {
  method_fig_dir <- .analysis_fig_dir(c(fig_key, "method-figures"), root_dir)
  figure_methods <- c("StimGate", "F-beta", "Tailgate")
  figure_colours <- c(StimGate = "#0072B2", `F-beta` = "#D55E00", Tailgate = "#009E73")
  fit_titles <- c(cd44 = "Fitted on CD44+ cells", nonnaive = "Fitted on all non-naïve cells")
  cofactor <- scientific_settings$preprocessing$cofactor
  for (fit in names(fit_titles)) {
    cat("\n\n### ", fit_titles[[fit]], "\n\n", sep = "")
    for (population in c("CD4", "CD8")) {
      for (strain in c("C57", "BALB")) {
        label <- paste0(if (strain == "C57") "C57BL/6" else "BALB/c", " ", population)
        bivariate <- .omip111MethodFigureData(prepared_inputs, comparison_results,
          comparison_object$resultsNonNaive, strain, figure_methods, cofactor, fit, population)
        n_rows <- length(levels(bivariate$gates$row))
        path_bi <- file.path(method_fig_dir, paste0(fit, "-fit-bivariate-", population, "-", strain, ".png"))
        ggplot2::ggsave(path_bi, .omip111MethodsFigure(bivariate, cofactor, figure_colours),
          width = 34, height = 6.5 * n_rows + 2, units = "cm", dpi = 130, bg = "white")
        univariate <- .omip111UnivariateFigureData(prepared_inputs, comparison_results,
          comparison_object$resultsNonNaive, strain, figure_methods, cofactor, fit, population)
        path_uni <- file.path(method_fig_dir, paste0(fit, "-fit-univariate-", population, "-", strain, ".png"))
        ggplot2::ggsave(path_uni, .omip111UnivariateFigure(univariate, cofactor, figure_colours),
          width = 34, height = 5.5 * n_rows + 2, units = "cm", dpi = 130, bg = "white")
        for (kind in c("Bivariate", "Univariate")) {
          path <- if (kind == "Bivariate") path_bi else path_uni
          cat("<details><summary>", kind, ": ", label, "</summary>\n\n",
            "![", kind, " ", label, "](", knitr::image_uri(path), ")\n\n</details>\n\n", sep = "")
        }
      }
    }
  }
}
```

## Cell classification and frequency correlation

Classification uses only stimulated tubes; unstimulated tubes have no
responders. The manual reference is the authors' cytokine-by-CD44 gate on
each cytokine's CD44-high parent cells. Manual gates are an imperfect reference. The mouse table retains every
TP, FP, FN and TN count and each metric's denominator. The summary pools
counts within strain, population, marker and method, and reports medians over
mice with the number of defined mouse metrics. Failed comparator gates remain
missing and contribute only to intended coverage.

```{r}
#| label: classification-tables
#| results: asis
if (isTRUE(run_plots) && exists("comparison_results") && nrow(comparison_results) > 0L) {
  report_results <- comparison_results
  classification <- .omip111Classification(prepared_inputs, report_results)
  .analysis_report_table(classification, c(fig_key, "classification-mice.csv"),
    "Stimulated-cell classification against the imperfect manual reference for every mouse.", root_dir)
  .analysis_report_table(.omip111ClassificationSummary(classification),
    c(fig_key, "classification.csv"),
    "Pooled cell counts and metric medians over mice, with defined coverage and denominators.", root_dir)
}
```

Pearson correlation measures association and Lin concordance correlation
measures agreement with the imperfect manual reference. Both use net
frequencies, retaining negative values, across mice within strain, population
and marker, and pooled across strains and markers within each population.
The pooled rows combine different markers and strains and are descriptive.
The table records intended and finite pairs; correlations are missing with
fewer than three finite pairs or zero variance in either frequency.

**Summary by population.** Counts are summed over strains, markers and mice
within each population before the proportions are calculated; Pearson and
concordance correlations (CCC) are the pooled rows of the CSV. `n_defined`
counts outcomes with a usable gate, and `n_pairs` the finite frequency pairs.
The summary table follows the link to the full CSV.

```{r}
#| label: frequency-correlations
#| results: asis
if (isTRUE(run_plots) && exists("report_results") && nrow(report_results) > 0L) {
  correlations <- .omipFrequencyCorrelationTable(report_results,
    c("strain", "population", "marker"), "propBs", "manualBs", "population")
  .analysis_report_table(correlations, c(fig_key, "frequency-correlations.csv"),
    "Pearson and population-moment Lin concordance correlations against manual net frequencies.", root_dir)
  .omipAgreementKable(.omipAgreementOverview(classification, correlations, "population"))
}
```

### Thesis heatmaps and stacked scatter figures

F1 compares cell masks on the same stimulated cells against the supplied author
reference. Heatmaps show mean finite per-tube F1 and frequency PCC/CCC, with
finite/intended coverage saved alongside the figures. Structurally unmeasured
combinations stay blank; observed undefined scores are labelled NA. Viridis
matches Analysis 7. Scatter panels retain the existing frequency estimand and
cohort.

CCC measures agreement, so it penalises a constant offset from the reference
that Pearson ignores. With five mice per strain, the between-mouse spread of
net frequencies for one marker is small, so a constant offset of a few
percentage points pulls CCC far below Pearson. A single outlying mouse has the same effect.

```{r}
#| label: thesis-stacked-real-comparison
#| include: false
if (isTRUE(run_plots) && exists("classification") && nrow(classification) > 0L) {
  thesis_rows <- .omip111ThesisRows(report_results, classification)
  .omipThesisFigures(
    thesis_rows,
    .analysis_project_dir("cache", c("omip111", "thesis-drafts", "stacked"), root_dir),
    referenceLabel = "manual gating, author CD44-high cytokine gates"
  )
}
```


### Correlation heatmaps by fit and evaluation population

Pearson (PCC) and concordance (CCC) correlations of net (stimulated minus
control) frequencies with manual gating, across the five mice of each strain,
for every combination of fit and evaluation population:

| | Evaluated on CD44+ cells | Evaluated on all non-naïve cells |
|---|---|---|
| **Fitted on CD44+ cells** | A (the primary comparison above) | B |
| **Fitted on all non-naïve cells** | C | D |

The fit population only sets each method's threshold. Positives are always
the cells in the cytokine's CD44+ parent (the authors' CD44 restriction)
above the threshold; the CD44+ population is never inferred from the
cytokine gate. The evaluation population sets the denominator: the CD44+
parent (A, C) or every non-naïve cell (B, D), where CD44-low cells add to
the denominator but are never positive. Two manual references: the authors'
**bivariate** CD44-by-cytokine gate, and their cytokine cutoff alone within
the CD44+ parent (**univariate**). With the CD44 restriction applied to both,
they differ only through the rectangle's upper cytokine bound, which no cell
reaches, and its inclusive lower edge. A against C, and B against D, isolate
the effect of fitting the threshold with CD44-low cells included. Tables of every stratum are saved
as CSVs; print-size copies (standard palette) are kept in the projr cache
under `omip111/thesis-drafts/fit-eval-heatmaps/<reference>/<combination>/`.

```{r}
#| label: fit-eval-heatmaps
#| results: asis
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 7
#| fig-height: 6
if (isTRUE(run_plots)) {
  combos <- data.frame(
    id = c("A", "B", "C", "D"), fit = c("cd44", "cd44", "nonnaive", "nonnaive"),
    evaluate = c("cd44", "nonnaive", "cd44", "nonnaive")
  )
  population_titles <- c(cd44 = "CD44+", nonnaive = "all non-naïve")
  fit_eval <- list()
  for (reference in c("bivariate", "univariate")) {
    cat("\n\n#### Manual reference: ", reference, " gates\n\n", sep = "")
    for (i in seq_len(nrow(combos))) {
      combo <- combos[i, ]
      scored <- .omip111FitEval(prepared_inputs, comparison_results, comparison_object$resultsNonNaive,
        combo$fit, combo$evaluate, reference)
      fit_eval[[length(fit_eval) + 1L]] <- scored
      rows <- scored
      rows$condition <- rows$strain
      rows$reference <- 100 * rows$manualBs
      rows$estimate <- 100 * rows$propBs
      rows$f1 <- NA_real_
      rows$scatterEligible <- rows$referenceAccepted
      summary <- .omipThesisSummary(rows)
      slug <- paste0(combo$id, "-fit-", combo$fit, "-evaluate-", combo$evaluate)
      .analysis_report_table(summary$strata, c(fig_key, paste0("fit-eval-correlations-", slug, "-", reference, ".csv")),
        paste0(combo$id, ", ", reference, " reference: correlations and coverage per stratum."), root_dir)
      for (metric in c("pearson", "ccc")) {
        cat("\n\n##### ", combo$id, ": fitted on ", population_titles[[combo$fit]], ", evaluated on ",
          population_titles[[combo$evaluate]], " (", if (metric == "pearson") "PCC" else "CCC", ")\n\n", sep = "")
        p <- .omipThesisHeatmap(summary$strata, metric, "standard", .omip111ThesisMethodLabels,
          parseMethods = TRUE)
        print(p)
        .analysis_save_thesis_fig(p, file.path(
          .analysis_project_dir("cache", c("omip111", "thesis-drafts", "fit-eval-heatmaps", reference, slug), root_dir),
          paste0(metric, "-stacked")), 45 + 3 * 25)
      }
    }
  }
  .analysis_report_table(dplyr::bind_rows(fit_eval), c(fig_key, "fit-eval-frequencies.csv"),
    "Net frequencies for every fit, evaluation population and manual reference.", root_dir)
}
```

## Frequency agreement and signed errors

Each point represents one matched mouse and cytokine. The identity line marks
agreement with the authors' gates. The signed-error plots retain exact zeros
and negative net frequencies. No confidence intervals are inferred from the
80 marker/population outcomes.

```{r}
#| label: agreement-figures
#| results: asis
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 7
if (isTRUE(run_plots)) {
  figure_dir <- .analysis_fig_dir(c(fig_key, "agreement"), root_dir)
  # The shared method colours and shapes, keyed by this table's method labels.
  method_ids <- c("stimgate", "fbeta", "tailgate")
  method_colours <- stats::setNames(.analysis_method_colours[method_ids], .analysis_method_labels[method_ids])
  method_shapes <- stats::setNames(.analysis_method_shapes[method_ids], .analysis_method_labels[method_ids])
  for (population in c("CD4", "CD8")) {
    cat("\n\n### CD44-high ", population, "\n\n", sep = "")
    plot_data <- comparison_results[comparison_results$population == population & comparison_results$referenceAccepted, ]
    plot_data$method <- factor(plot_data$method, levels = names(method_colours))
    p <- ggplot2::ggplot(plot_data, ggplot2::aes(100 * manualBs, 100 * propBs,
      colour = method, shape = method)) +
      ggplot2::geom_abline(slope = 1, intercept = 0, colour = "grey60") +
      ggplot2::geom_point(size = 1.7, alpha = 0.5, na.rm = TRUE) +
      ggplot2::facet_wrap(ggplot2::vars(strain, marker), scales = "free", ncol = 5) +
      ggplot2::scale_colour_manual(values = method_colours) +
      ggplot2::scale_shape_manual(values = method_shapes) +
      ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(labels = .analysis_label_number) +
      ggplot2::scale_x_continuous(labels = .analysis_label_number) +
      ggplot2::labs(x = "Background-subtracted frequency\n(manual gating, %)",
        y = "Background-subtracted frequency\n(automated gating, %)", colour = NULL, shape = NULL) +
      .analysis_theme()
    print(p)
    ggplot2::ggsave(file.path(figure_dir, paste0(population, "-frequency-agreement.png")), p,
      width = 10, height = 7, units = "in", dpi = 150)
    p_error <- ggplot2::ggplot(plot_data, ggplot2::aes(method, errorPp, colour = method)) +
      ggplot2::geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey60") +
      ggplot2::geom_point(ggplot2::aes(group = mouse), position = ggplot2::position_dodge(width = 0.4),
        size = 1.7, alpha = 0.5, na.rm = TRUE) +
      ggplot2::facet_wrap(ggplot2::vars(strain, marker), scales = "free_y", ncol = 5) +
      .analysis_y_floor(c(-10, 10)) +
      ggplot2::scale_colour_manual(values = method_colours) +
      ggplot2::scale_y_continuous(labels = .analysis_label_number) +
      ggplot2::labs(x = NULL, y = "Automated − manual background-subtracted\nfrequency (percentage points)", colour = NULL) +
      .analysis_theme() + ggplot2::theme(axis.text.x = ggplot2::element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1))
    print(p_error)
    ggplot2::ggsave(file.path(figure_dir, paste0(population, "-signed-error.png")), p_error,
      width = 10, height = 7, units = "in", dpi = 150)
  }
}
```

## Investigate individual gates

These are the same diagnostic panels used for ACS in Analysis 13, for **every
mouse, population and marker**, for both fit populations: the CD44+ fit (the
primary comparison) and the fit on all non-naïve cells. Expand a mouse below to inspect the control and
stimulated densities, response probability and its derivative, expected responding
cells per bin, and taut-string/filter boundaries. The lines overlay the initial
gate, the final StimGate gate and conditional cytokine-positive gate, F-beta,
Tailgate, and the actual author cytokine lower cutoffs transformed to `asinh(raw / 150)`.
Overlapping stimulated/control author cutoffs can appear as one line.

The purple author lines are the cytokine side of the authors' cytokine-by-CD44
rectangles. On CD44+ pages the CD44 side defines the parent cells, and the
result block gives the saved frequencies over that parent (combination A). On
non-naïve pages the densities are of every non-naïve cell, and the result
block gives frequencies over every non-naïve cell (combination D: CD44+
cells above the gate, over every non-naïve cell), against the authors' gate
counted over the same cells. All samples
are rerun together with the original settings and seed, to preserve gate
sharing: within each strain, population and cytokine for the CD44+ fit, and
within each strain and population for the non-naïve fit.
Both final base and conditional gates must exactly reproduce the saved comparison
before any pages are published. Each PDF contains all five mice for its marker and fit.

`RUN_DIAGNOSTICS=true` regenerates these panels without requiring preprocessing
or comparator refitting. Set `RUN_DIAGNOSTICS=false` to reuse validated pages.

```{r}
#| label: individual-gate-diagnostics
#| results: asis
#| echo: false
#| out-width: 100%
if (isTRUE(run_plots)) {
  diagnostic_dir <- .analysis_fig_dir(c(fig_key, "gate-diagnostics"), root_dir)
  if (run_diagnostics) {
    .acsCytofEnsureCurrentCheckout(root_dir)
    .omip111DebugRun(prepared_inputs, comparison_results, scientific_settings,
      diagnostic_dir, path_results, comparison_object$resultsNonNaive)
  }
  if (!file.exists(file.path(diagnostic_dir, "COMPLETE"))) stop("Gate diagnostics are missing; use RUN_DIAGNOSTICS=true.")
  diagnostic_object <- readRDS(file.path(diagnostic_dir, "diagnostics.rds"))
  if (!identical(diagnostic_object$settings, scientific_settings) ||
    !identical(diagnostic_object$context, prepared_inputs$manifest)) {
    stop("Saved gate diagnostics are stale; use RUN_DIAGNOSTICS=true.")
  }
  diagnostic_index <- diagnostic_object$index
  .analysis_report_table(diagnostic_index, c(fig_key, "gate-diagnostic-index.csv"),
    "All 160 diagnostic pages (80 per fit population), with PDF page numbers and saved-gate parity.", root_dir)
  .omip111DiagnosticPages(diagnostic_index, diagnostic_dir)
}
```

## Observed agreement

All three methods completed 80 outcomes without runtime errors or threshold
fallbacks. Two C57 mouse 2 CD8 references (IFNγ and TNF) miss FlowJo's
frequency by 0.11 percentage points and are not scored, leaving 78 per method.

Tailgate's near-zero frequencies for TNF and IL-2 in both populations (apart
from BALB CD8 IL-2, which is far too low but not zero) are calculated
cutpoints, not fallbacks. Tailgate starts from the highest
density peak of the stimulated tube, finds the steepest point of its right
shoulder, and cuts at the first point beyond it where the density's slope falls
below 1% of its largest absolute slope. For CD4 TNF the highest peak is the
responding population itself, and for the other cases the responders form a
long shoulder rather than a separate peak with a flat valley before it. In
both cases the slope never flattens within the data, so the first flat point
lies beyond the brightest cell and the gate excludes almost every cell. Where a
second peak creates a valley (CD4 IFNγ), Tailgate gates normally.

No events in these parent populations exceed the authors' cytokine upper extents.


```{r}
#| label: observed-agreement
#| results: asis
if (isTRUE(run_plots)) {
  descriptive_errors <- comparison_results |>
    dplyr::group_by(.data$method) |>
    dplyr::summarise(eligible_outcomes = sum(is.finite(.data$errorPp)),
      mean_absolute_error_pp = mean(.data$absoluteErrorPp, na.rm = TRUE),
      median_absolute_error_pp = stats::median(.data$absoluteErrorPp, na.rm = TRUE),
      .groups = "drop")
  cat("Descriptive errors across retained marker/population outcomes, in percentage points. ",
    "Outcomes from one mouse are repeated measurements; these averages do not provide independent-replicate confidence intervals.\n\n", sep = "")
  print(knitr::kable(descriptive_errors, digits = 3))
}
```

OMIP-111 is useful as an external agreement dataset and a stress test of
background matching. A lower pooled error on this small panel should not be
interpreted as general method superiority. Restricting both tubes to each
cytokine gate's CD44 interval removes the stimulation-induced change in the
non-naïve gate and matches the authors' CD44 restriction. Transformation
sensitivity and expert review remain appropriate
before claims about biological accuracy.

## Interpretation limits

The full CSV companions retain per-mouse, per-marker results and all missing
outcomes. Agreement with manual gating supports external plausibility; it
cannot establish biological sensitivity or false discovery rate. The CD44-high
parents hold only about 650–5,600 cells per tube, so sparse cytokines
(IL-17A, IL-4/5) rest on a handful of cells. The two mouse strains, five mice
per strain, one acquisition setting and mitogen stimulus provide a bounded
external validation rather than a representative survey of use cases.
